How many products the graphs allow (small models)

Source: R/configuration.R
vp_count_graph_products.Rd

How many products the graphs allow, by trying every selection of the variable features. Only for small models (max_features, 20 by default). It shows how much of the model the graphs capture: compare the last number with the number of valid configurations of the model, when it is known.

Usage

vp_count_graph_products(model, max_features = 20, products = NULL)

Arguments

model

A model, from vp_generate() or vp_read(), in its complete or its minimal form.

max_features

The largest number of variable features to try (2^n selections).

products

The number of valid products of the model, if you know it (from a model counter): then two more columns say how much of the model the graphs explain, on a scale of yes/no choices (bits).

Value

One row: selections (2^n), respect_requires, and_excludes, and_atleastone (NA without or_graph = TRUE); with products, also bits_model (how many of the n yes/no choices the model takes away: n - log2(products)) and explained (the share of them that the graphs take away).

See also

Other configuration: vp_can_go_together(), vp_consequences(), vp_kernel(), vp_kernel_links(), vp_mig(), vp_most_decisive(), vp_pair(), vp_partial_configuration(), vp_rounds(), vp_split_after(), vp_splitting_decisions(), vp_team_links(), vp_team_moves(), vp_team_order(), vp_teams()

Examples

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
vp_count_graph_products(band)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   selections respect_requires and_excludes and_atleastone
#>        <dbl>            <int>        <int>          <int>
#> 1       2048               34           12             10
